findings.claim: Title "Exposure-Mapping Fidelity Governs Accuracy"; abstract: "0.031--0.054 whenever the fitted mapping matches the generating form ... and 0.151--0.452 when it does not"; conclusion: "When the mapping did not match (saturating, degree-dependent and two-hop responses)"
findings.evidence: paper.tex Method (frozen estimator paragraph) and Bias/variance section ("gate diagnostics were not verified"); paper_data.json final_evaluation.evaluation_evidence.candidate_diagnostics_trust="unverified"; claims_grounding.json has no claim that supports a mapping-match or causal-governance statement, only per-case RMSE values; Limitations items (3), (5), (6).
findings.fix: Change the title and abstract to descriptive, hedged wording, for example "per-case error was low in the five cases whose generating form is linear in the neighbour fraction and higher in the saturating, count-by-degree and two-hop cases". Remove "whenever the fitted mapping matches" and "when it does not", and state that mapping selection and fidelity were not verified and that the mapping-fidelity account is a hypothesis.
findings.issue: The manuscript states as established fact that the fitted mapping matched in cases 1-5 and mismatched in cases 6-8, and that fidelity governs error. But the paper itself says the per-case gate decisions were not logged in verified form, so it cannot report which mapping was selected in any case. The library contained a sigmoid centred at 0.5 with scale 0.1, which is the case-6 generating form, so a mismatch there is not shown. The design is non-factorial, per-case baseline and oracle values are unavailable, and the cause of the two-hop failure is explicitly unknown. The body hedges, but the title, abstract and conclusion assert the cause.

findings.claim: Frozen estimator details: "15 mappings", BIC margin of 10, winsorising at three times the 99.5th percentile, three-times-max fallback rule, HC1 delta-method intervals, "does not use the design description". Also the flexible-ensemble and residual-correction descriptions, the HT inclusion probabilities, the oracle feature lists, and "ignores cluster dependence under the cluster design and uses no resampling".
findings.evidence: ls /workspace shows no source_evidence directory; claims_grounding.json claims[0-15] cover only metrics and references; paper_data.json final_evaluation.evaluation_evidence.candidate_diagnostics_trust="unverified"; paper.tex Supplementary "Source: the estimator source file ..."
findings.fix: Remove these implementation specifics, or qualify them as the authors' description that the audit could not inspect. Keep only the details grounded in the evaluator metrics. Drop the statement that the interval ignores cluster dependence and uses no resampling, and the specific descriptions of the two alternative estimators and the HT and oracle internals.
findings.issue: These implementation-specific claims cite "the estimator source file ... functions candidate_designs, bic_gate and _estimate", but no ./source_evidence/ directory exists in the workspace. claims_grounding.json contains no claim covering any of them, and the final-evaluation candidate diagnostics are marked unverified. Hashes in paper_data.json show provenance only, not support for the details.
findings.section: Method (Compared estimators), Supplementary Estimator and Baseline Definitions, Supplementary Model-Selection Comparison, Reliability

findings.claim: Model-selection per-case errors, bias and coverage for the three estimator classes, plus baselines 0.184/0.623/0.925/0.050, and "library case 6 0.267 vs 0.708 ... case 7 0.183 vs 0.098 ... case 8 0.445/0.428"
findings.evidence: paper_data.json grounding_sources result.improvement_00x (value only); claims_grounding.json claims for "Model-selection plane" and "Per-case model-selection errors"; search_plane_metrics/estimator_0{1,2,3}_metrics.json; paper.tex Table 2 @evidence comments.
findings.fix: Ground Table 2 and the model-selection per-case claims to the search_plane_metrics source ids. If they cannot be registered, describe these values only as search-set diagnostics and reduce the claims to the plane-level scores that result.improvement_* support.
findings.issue: claims_grounding.json grounds these claims to result.improvement_001/002/003, result.best_correct_score and result.total_attempts. In paper_data.json those sources hold only the scalar plane score (-0.232, -0.185, -0.140). They contain no per-case values, bias, coverage or baseline values. The per-case numbers come from search_plane_metrics/estimator_0X_metrics.json, which is not a registered grounding source id, and the paper's anchored @evidence refs to those files are not reflected in the claims ledger. The values do match those files, but the cited source ids do not support the visible Table 2 and the per-case contrasts.
findings.section: Results (Bias, variance and the gated library), Table 2, Supplementary Model-Selection Comparison

findings.claim: Node-relabelled graph relative RMSE 0.627 is "close to DiM's 0.622: once the exposure features are scrambled, regression recovers only the direct effect, which indicates that the estimator is using the real graph"
findings.evidence: claims_grounding.json claim on controls (final.metric.control_permuted_graph_rmse_rel only); paper_data.json candidate_diagnostics_trust="unverified"; paper.tex Validity checks paragraph and Supplementary controls paragraph.
findings.fix: Report the 0.627 control value and the 0.622 DiM value as numbers, and note that they are similar. Delete the "recovers only the direct effect" explanation and soften "indicates that the estimator is using the real graph" to a statement that the relabelled-graph error is much larger than the 0.126 headline.
findings.issue: Only the numbers 0.627 and 0.622 are grounded. The claim that the estimator "recovers only the direct effect" and the inference that the estimator "is using the real graph" are mechanistic interpretations that no evaluator evidence supports. The paper also says the estimator's per-case behaviour and gate decisions were not inspected or verified. Similar values of two different quantities do not establish that mechanism.
findings.section: Results (Validity checks) and Supplementary Negative Controls

summary: The reported numbers match paper_data.json, derived_stats.json and search_plane_metrics, but the implementation details are not grounded, and the headline wording asserts a mapping-fidelity cause that the evidence cannot show.
